Budget notes:

- Beans, lentils, eggs, peanut butter, yogurt, milk, and tuna/chicken provide affordable protein.
- Oats, brown rice, whole wheat bread, beans, lentils, apples, cabbage, carrots, and potatoes provide fiber and steady energy.
- Frozen vegetables help maintain micronutrient intake with less spoilage risk.
- Milk, yogurt, and cheese support calcium intake; choose fortified alternatives if dairy is not tolerated.
- Use low-sodium canned goods when possible, and rinse canned beans to reduce sodium.

- Items are generally available at discount grocery stores, supermarkets, and many dollar-format food retailers.
- Most meals require only basic equipment: pot, skillet, microwave or stovetop, knife, and storage containers.
- Batch-cook rice, beans/lentils, and chopped vegetables once or twice weekly to reduce time pressure.
